biography.plain_text: Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed Al Nahyan was the UAE's second president and ruler of Abu Dhabi from 2004 until his death in 2022. The eldest son of founding president Sheikh Zayed, he led Abu Dhabi's first local cabinet and held its defence and finance portfolios. He served as deputy supreme commander of the armed forces.

long_biography.plain_text:
Raised in Al Ain, Khalifa bin Zayed Al Nahyan learned government by accompanying his father among the communities of the Eastern Region and attending his public majlis. In 1966, he became the Abu Dhabi ruler's representative there and head of its legal system, combining administration with agricultural and infrastructure projects.

As chairman of the Abu Dhabi Executive Council, he oversaw housing, roads and water systems. He also helped establish the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority to invest government funds for the emirate's future. During his presidency, the first Federal National Council elections were introduced, followed by a later directive that women occupy half its seats. He remained president until his death in May 2022.
long_biography.html:
Raised in Al Ain, Khalifa bin Zayed Al Nahyan learned government by accompanying his father among the communities of the Eastern Region and attending his public majlis. In 1966, he became the Abu Dhabi ruler's representative there and head of its legal system, combining administration with agricultural and infrastructure projects.

As chairman of the Abu Dhabi Executive Council, he oversaw housing, roads and water systems. He also helped establish the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority to invest government funds for the emirate's future. During his presidency, the first Federal National Council elections were introduced, followed by a later directive that women occupy half its seats. He remained president until his death in May 2022.
